chunks: My father (rah) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, saying: Uthman ibn Isa narrated to me from al-'Ala ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said:

Imam al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon him) said to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): 'O father, what is the reward for one who visits you, what is the reward?' He (peace be upon him and his family) replied: 'For one who visits me, or visits your father, or visits you, or visits your brother, it is obligatory upon me to visit him on the Day of Judgment until I free him from his sins.'

key_terms.أُخَلِّصَهُ: I will free him / absolve him

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting the Prophet and Imams according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal*, Imam al-Hasan ibn Ali (a.s.) conveys the Prophet’s promise that visiting him or his Ahl al-Bayt guarantees divine intercession on the Day of Judgment. This highlights the Shia concept of *Ziyarat* not merely as a physical act, but as a spiritual bond where the Imam actively participates in the visitor’s purification from sins, reflecting the unique status of the Imams as mediators of God's mercy.
